subject: Post-call: Stakeholder roles, procurement path & steering committee onramp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lena Brooks <lena.brooks@gridlytics.com>; TJ Chen <tj.chen@gridlytics.com>; procurement@gridlytics.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:10:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Stakeholder roles, procurement path & steering committee onramp

Hi Lena / TJ — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same picture: 

Summary (from today’s discovery):
- Primary usage: near-real-time inference for product personalization (low-100s qps, 64-token average).
- Must-haves: 99th-pct latency <= 120ms, on-prem data residency for PII workloads, SOC 2 attestation, and predictable unit economics.
- Decision criteria called out by the panel: TCO over 24 months, latency SLOs, security evidence, and integration effort.

Identified stakeholders from your side:
- Economic buyer / Sponsor: Lena Brooks (VP Product) — will own budget and go/no-go.
- Security / Compliance: TJ Chen — will run SOC 2 + data residency assessment.
- Procurement: procurement@gridlytics.com — commercial terms and contracting.
- Technical reviewers: Engineering + Infra (names TBD).

Proposed next steps / ask items (owner / ETA):
1) Schedule a 30–45 min steering committee call next week with the sponsor (Lena) + our exec sponsor (Karthik). Ben to propose times — ACTION: Ben — by EOD 12/1.
2) TJ to share the security checklist and any required evidence types (logs, audit config, certs) — ACTION: TJ — by 12/3.
3) Procurement to confirm standard PO/legal intake and Redlines window — ACTION: procurement@gridlytics.com — by 12/4.
4) We’ll send a short ROI worksheet + an initial SOW draft for procurement/legal review — ATTACHMENTS: redwood-mag-roi-worksheet.xlsx, sow-draft-v0.2.docx — ACTION: Ben/Monica — sent below.

If that aligns, I’ll propose two steering committee slots for next week (Weds 12/8 10:00–10:45 PT or Thurs 12/9 11:00–11:45 PT). Please confirm preferred slot or propose alternatives.

Thanks again — excited to keep the momentum.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-mag-roi-worksheet.xlsx (ROI worksheet), sow-draft-v0.2.docx (initial SOW draft)

Date: 2026-12-02T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Stakeholder roles, procurement path & steering committee onramp

Ben — thanks for the tidy recap. That matches our notes. A few clarifying points: 

- I can commit to being on a single steering call to make the budget decision, likely following a technical sign-off.
- TJ will lead the security review; he’ll need to see the SOC2 evidence and any details about network flows for on-prem components.
- Procurement: our team needs an initial SOW + sample commercial terms. We generally run 2–3 weeks of review for standard SaaS-ish contracts (shorter for fixed price/commitments).

I prefer Thurs 12/9 11:00–11:45 PT for the steering call. If you can get Karthik on, that would be ideal — he can speak to pricing tradeoffs.

I’ll loop in a named eng reviewer after I check calendars (should have that by EOD 12/3).

—
Lena Brooks
VP Product, GridLytics
lena.brooks@gridlytics.com

Thanks — good alignment. A few operational items on our side to make the steering meeting productive: 

Prep pack (we will circulate ahead of the meeting):
- One-pager exec summary (2 slides): value, ask, recommended configuration and high-level price bands.
- Short runbook for the security review: what TJ will receive and timelines (I’ll attach SOC2-evidence-request.pdf).
- ROI worksheet filled with our top-line assumptions (I’ll tidy Ben’s spreadsheet).
- Initial SOW highlights with optional purchase configurations (commit vs. burst).

Ben — can you confirm the configuration you used in the ROI worksheet (concurrency, perf SLOs, quantization profile)? That will drive the price bands we show.
Karthik — can you join the steering call as Redwood’s exec sponsor? We’ve found sponsor-to-sponsor alignment materially shortens procurement cycles.
Marissa — once seats are confirmed, can you prepare a 5–7 minute demo snippet focused on cold-start latency and KV cache behavior for the steering call? Keep it high level.

I’ve attached SOC2-evidence-request.pdf to this thread for TJ and the GridLytics procurement/security teams.

—
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Thanks team — I’ll be there for the steering call on 12/9 11:00 PT. A couple of priorities before the meeting: 

1) Tighten the decision criteria into a short evaluation matrix (we should list must/should/want):
   - Must: SOC2, latency 99p <= 120ms, data residency for PII workloads
   - Should: 24-month TCO <= $X (we’ll set the band), predictable burst policy for holiday traffic
   - Want: native integrations to our SSO and observability stack

2) Commercial ask: I’d like to present two pricing options in the deck — committed throughput with a lower unit cost, and a flexible burst option. We should show modeled spend for Q1 and Q2. Ben/Monica please put those on the ROI worksheet.

3) For procurement/legal: highlight any non-standard clauses early (data residency, audit right windows). If GridLytics has a standard SLAs appendix, get that to Marissa and me ahead of the call.

I’ll review the SOW draft by EOD 12/4 and send comments.

—
Karthik Iyer
SVP, Commercial | Redwood Inference
